content: The American Social Health Association (ASHA) is a non-profit organization based in the United States. It was established in the early 20th century and remains actively involved in addressing issues related to sexually transmitted diseases (STDs). ASHA's origins can be traced back to the Progressive Era's social purity movement. In 1911, two prominent purity organizations, the American Purity Alliance and the American Vigilance Committee, merged to form the American Vigilance Association. Around the same time, in 1910, groups with a stronger focus on medical approaches elected Prince A. Morrow as the president of the American Federation for Sex Hygiene. Following the death of Prince A. Morrow in 1913, the two organizations, along with their respective ideologies, united to create the American Social Hygiene Association. This organization was renamed in 1914 to the American Social Health Association. One of the key influential figures in the early development of ASHA was John D. Rockefeller, Jr.
